idea: Wrong-side ledger — for every closed losing trade, compute reverse-direction PnL (entry->exit flipped) and persist to a table
rationale: Fundamental truth: every losing trade means someone else gained what we lost. Currently we only know OUR pnl. A reverse-PnL column would quantify how often losses were (a) wrong-side (reverse would have won big) vs (b) right-side bad-exit (reverse would have lost too). LDO pump-chain+ LONG lost -$0.14 in STRONG_DOWN — reverse SHORT would have gained. IO pump-chain- SHORT at meta RSI 41 lost — reverse LONG (the oversold bounce) was the winning side. Without this metric we cannot systematically separate "wrong direction" from "right direction, bad exit."
expected_impact: Enables wrong-side ratio as first-class KPI. Targets signal-quality fixes at direction errors, not just exit tuning. Feeds the fundamental-truth mandate directly.
implementation: On trade close, lookup same coin price path entry->exit; reverse_pnl = -pnl_usdt * (direction==LONG ? 1 : 1) wait — reverse means if we were LONG, hypothetical SHORT entry at our entry price closed at our exit price. Store reverse_pnl_usdt. Shadow-only, no trading path impact.
